data.title: Arcturus targets Q4 2026 Phase III decision for ARCT-032 as it regains global KOSTAIVE rights
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Arcturus Therapeutics (ARCT) Q2 2026

Management View

  • CEO Joseph Payne said Q2 2026 featured “continued execution across our rare disease pipeline and important strategic developments for Arcturus' vaccine franchise,” highlighting a Q4 2026 decision point for CF and a Q3 2026 data update for OTC deficiency.

  • On cystic fibrosis, CEO Payne said the Phase II ARCT-032 study continued “on schedule with active screening and enrollment ongoing across sites in the United States, Israel, and Turkey,” and reiterated that “the decision to advance our CF program into Phase III is expected in the fourth quarter, or Q4 2026,” with Thermo Fisher support triggered if Arcturus proceeds.

  • On OTC deficiency, CEO Payne said Arcturus “completed enrollment in our ongoing Phase II study, and all enrolled subjects have completed study drug dosing,” and added, “We expect to communicate the Phase II clinical study data later this year in Q3 2026,” alongside an update on the regulatory path forward.

  • On vaccines, CEO Payne announced, “Today we announced the conclusion of our sa-mRNA collaboration with CSL Seqirus,” adding Arcturus is “pleased to regain global rights to our commercial COVID vaccine product, KOSTAIVE, and to our self-amplifying mRNA platform,” and said the settlement included “a one-time cash payment of $12 million” and release from liabilities “with an aggregate value of approximately $16 million.”

  • CFO Dennis Mulroy reported, “Cash and cash equivalents were $191.5 million as of June 30, 2026,” and said, “We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet and cash runway of over 2.5 years through year-end 2028.”

Outlook

  • Management framed near-term catalysts around program decisions rather than quantified revenue/EPS guidance; no explicit revenue or EPS guidance was provided in the prepared remarks.

  • CEO Payne set the CF timeline as a decision event: “our new guidance is focusing on the decision to proceed rather than a data share or completion of enrollment,” and said the “next meaningful event for this program is that decision, which is guided for Q4.”

  • For OTC, CEO Payne said the Q3 2026 update is intended to be “a fulsome update on the OTC program that includes not only the Phase II data, but the requested Type C data, and providing additional detail with respect to the regulatory path forward.”

  • For the regained vaccine portfolio, CEO Payne said Arcturus is “evaluating opportunities to maximize its future value, including further commercialization and partnering pathways,” with Japan operations “very active right now with Meiji” ahead of the fall season.

Financial Results

  • CFO Mulroy reported revenue of $3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and said the decline versus last year reflected “Lower revenue … under the CSL collaboration as Arcturus progressed towards termination of the agreement and regaining rights to KOSTAIVE.”

  • CFO Mulroy reported R&D expense of $17.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, attributing the decrease primarily to “reduced salaries, wages, benefits, and facilities costs,” while maintaining a “disciplined approach to capital allocation.”

  • CFO Mulroy reported G&A expense of $11 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, saying it was “relatively consistent” with a “slight quarter-to-quarter increase due to legal fees.”

Q&A

  • Lili Nsongo, Leerink Partners: asked what to expect in the upcoming OTC readout (U.S. vs. Europe) and whether success hinges on diet liberalization vs biomarkers; CEO Payne said the update will include “the U.S. and European dataset” and “supplementary data … requested by the FDA,” while CMO Alan Cohen said endpoints will reflect “the totality of the data,” including “safety and tolerability … biomarkers … most notably ammonia levels and glutamine … [and] quality of life and functional measures.”

  • Pete Stavropoulos, Cantor Fitzgerald: asked about CF enrollment cadence, interim looks, and extending dosing; CEO Payne said management has “a high level of confidence with respect to the cadence of enrollment rate now that Israel and Turkey are participating,” while CMO Cohen said timing should allow enough data “through a balance of Q4” for the Phase III decision.

  • Kuan-Hung Lin, Wells Fargo: asked what dataset supports the Q4 CF decision and whether the open-label design means real-time visibility, plus any safety signals; CEO Payne said Arcturus will consider FEV1, LCI, high-resolution CT, and quality-of-life measures, confirmed “we will have access to data on an ongoing basis,” and added ARCT-032 has been in “over 50 participants to date” with “a high level of confidence in our safety and tolerability.”

  • Joohwan Kim, Citigroup: asked how the Thermo Fisher deal came about and whether Thermo saw interim data; CEO Payne said there was “significant interest from multiple large manufacturers,” and confirmed, “they had access to all the data.”

  • Jake Batchelder, William Blair: asked about hyperammonemic crisis rates in OTC and the U.S. regulatory path for KOSTAIVE; CMO Cohen said the Phase II design is “not looking to capture patients that are unstable enough” for frequent events, while CEO Payne said Arcturus has received “very clear guidance as to what is needed for us to get this approved in the U.S.”

  • Whitney Ijem, Canaccord: asked what quantitative CF endpoints could justify Phase III and about Japan economics post-CSL; CEO Payne said thresholds will be established “by us in this process,” and said Japan was previously a “three ways” profit split that “will be split two ways,” with details under discussion with Meiji.

  • Jinnie Kim, BTIG: asked whether regaining global vaccine rights changes cost/R&D trajectory; CEO Payne emphasized monetization via “commercialization” and “partnership,” pointing to portfolio targets including “seasonal flu and pandemic flu … RSV, and EBV.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and detail-seeking, pressing for clarity on decision criteria and regulatory steps, including questions on CF interim visibility and what endpoints could drive Phase III.

  • Management tone was slightly positive and milestone-focused, repeatedly anchoring to specific upcoming events (Q3 OTC data and Q4 CF proceed/no-proceed decision) and pointing to strategic value from regaining vaccine rights.

  • Versus Q1 2026, management discussion shifted from emphasizing early tolerability milestones in CF to emphasizing a formal Q4 2026 Phase III decision trigger tied to Thermo Fisher contributions, while analyst questions expanded to include the post-CSL vaccine strategy.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q2 introduced a major strategic change versus Q1: CEO Payne announced the CSL Seqirus collaboration concluded and Arcturus “regain[ed] global rights” to KOSTAIVE and the broader infectious disease portfolio, alongside a $12 million cash payment and release from approximately $16 million of liabilities.

  • In CF, Q1 emphasized being “well beyond one month of dosing” as a tolerability milestone; in Q2, CEO Payne emphasized that “the next meaningful event … is that decision” in Q4 2026, with communication centered on proceeding to Phase III rather than interim disclosure.

  • In OTC, Q1 highlighted FDA direction and exploratory data needs; Q2 advanced operationally to “completed enrollment” and “completed study drug dosing,” and management set expectations to share Phase II data and the regulatory plan in Q3 2026.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management emphasized that inhaled therapeutics face tolerability challenges, with CEO Payne saying, “Humans just don't like to inhale foreign substances,” and framed ARCT-032’s differentiators as a “biodegradable, non-accumulating” lipid nanoparticle, a purification process to control inflammatory impurities, and an optimized nebulizer.

  • Analysts repeatedly probed uncertainty around open-label interpretation, endpoint thresholds, and timing of disclosures; management’s mitigation was to rely on a multi-measure dataset (FEV1, LCI, CT, quality of life) and to wait for a “larger body of data” before detailed tolerability commentary.

Final Takeaway

Management positioned the quarter around two near-term rare-disease milestones—ARCT-810 Phase II data and a regulatory path update in Q3 2026, and a Q4 2026 decision on whether to advance ARCT-032 into Phase III—while also reframing Arcturus’ longer-term opportunity set by ending the CSL Seqirus collaboration, regaining global rights to KOSTAIVE and a broader infectious disease portfolio, and pursuing commercialization and partnering options for the validated sa-mRNA platform.

data.title: Outset Medical reiterates $125M-$130M 2026 revenue guidance backed by $40M HCA refresh agreement
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Outset Medical (OM) Q2 2026

Management View

  • “The second quarter reflected steady execution across revenue, gross margin, operating expense discipline, and cash management,” said Leslie Trigg (President, CEO & Chairman), citing revenue of “$31.6 million” and reiterating “full year 2026 revenue guidance of $125 million to $130 million.”

  • Trigg highlighted implementation and customer expansion momentum, saying Outset “completed our highest number of successful new site implementations in several years,” and described a customer success model where “each hospital customer is paired with a clinical excellence team member” supported by “Tablo's unique data ecosystem.”

  • Trigg announced, “We are privileged to have signed a $40 million refresh agreement with HCA Healthcare,” adding that the commitment “extends through 2028,” is Outset’s “first refresh win,” and is tied to a refresh cycle that “may include roughly 3,000 consoles and up to $150 million in console revenue opportunity.”

  • Renee Gaeta (CFO, Principal Financial Officer & Principal Accounting Officer) said, “Second quarter non-GAAP gross margin was 42.2%, up over 380 basis points compared to last year,” and added, “we ended the quarter with $151 million in cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, and restricted cash.”

Outlook

  • Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance. Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) said, “we continue to expect full year revenue of $125 million to $130 million… with most of the growth expected in the third and fourth quarters,” and attributed confidence to “a strong commercial pipeline and the foundational contracted backlog provided by the HCA refresh agreement.”

  • Compared with last quarter’s messaging, management shifted from next-gen Tablo “initial transition… later this quarter” and “limited release” language to a more measured rollout posture. Trigg (CEO Trigg) said, “We're working on the pilot phase now in preparation for a successful broader launch,” and in Q&A added, “we obviously want to make sure we really, really, really get this right… focus on doing it well versus quickly.”

Financial Results

  • Q2 revenue was $31.6M vs. $28.8M (analysts’ revenue estimate).

  • Revenue mix and profitability drivers were framed around consoles, recurring revenue, and margin programs. Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) reported product revenue of $21.9M, including console revenue of $9.5M and consumable revenue of $12.4M; service and other revenue was $9.7M. She also reported recurring revenue of $22.1M.

  • Margin and cost discipline were tied to a stated profitability path. Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) reported non-GAAP operating expenses of $25.8M and non-GAAP operating loss of $12.4M, while saying gross margin performance “keeps us on track towards our next milestone of a 50% company-wide gross margin.”

  • Cash burn commentary remained a key investor focus. Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) said, “cash use was $9.5 million… keeping us on track to use less than $40 million in cash for the full year.”

Q&A

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: Asked what drove console revenue strength and how much was tied to HCA vs. other factors; Renee Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) said “HCA was a part of our Q2 pipeline and a part of our strong console performance,” while adding Outset also had “new expansion customers” and a “broad range within our pipeline,” and Leslie Trigg (CEO Trigg) said she was “very pleased to see the distribution” between “current customer expansion” and “new customer acquisition,” with “green shoots” from refresh, customer success, and leadership changes.

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: Pressed on consumable revenue decline and whether it signaled weakening demand; Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) pointed to “a tough comparable” from 2025, “flu season and census” effects, and ordering cadence, and said Outset sees “strong utilization” with “nothing alarming,” while Trigg (CEO Trigg) added delayed implementations are now flowing through and Outset has “pristine” utilization visibility because Tablo transmits data “after every treatment, every day.”

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: Asked how to think about second-half cadence given the Q2 upside; Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) cited “an element of seasonality” in Q3 and said “Q4 is a stronger quarter for us,” and Trigg (CEO Trigg) added “positive seasonality on the capital sales side” as hospitals spend budgets before year-end.

  • Brian (for Josh Jennings), TD Cowen: Asked about phasing of the HCA agreement and whether 2027 is the largest year; Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) declined to split 2027/2028 timing, saying the company has “visibility to 2026,” will provide “2027 guidance at the appropriate time,” and emphasized a broader “robust pipeline” and additional refresh opportunities.

  • Brian (for Josh Jennings), TD Cowen: Asked about next-gen Tablo feedback and milestones to full launch; Trigg (CEO Trigg) said customer discussions show “a lot of enthusiasm” driven by cybersecurity needs, and said Outset will use pilot metrics to confirm “the user experience… performance of the system, and the performance of the update” before full rollout.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive but probing on sustainability and cadence, emphasizing variability and phasing; Wise highlighted console revenue being “nicely above” expectations and then pressed whether it was “a one-time pull forward,” while also calling the consumables question “a fair one.”

  • Management tone was slightly positive and more guarded on timing details, leaning on confidentiality and pilot discipline; Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) repeatedly cited “customer confidentiality reasons,” and Trigg (CEO Trigg) emphasized measured execution: “focus on doing it well versus quickly.”

  • Versus last quarter, management sounded less specific on next-gen launch timing (moving from limited release language to pilot/quality emphasis), while analysts shifted attention from Q1 “lumpiness” to Q2 upside drivers, consumables softness, and HCA revenue phasing.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • The largest strategic change was the move from discussing an “emerging refresh opportunity” (Q1) to announcing a specific deal: “a $40 million refresh agreement with HCA Healthcare” (Q2), which management said adds “contracted backlog” and “visibility.”

  • Next-gen Tablo messaging evolved from Q1 rollout timing (“limited release… then ramp to a full launch”) to Q2 execution control, with Trigg emphasizing pilot validation and reluctance to share competitive details.

  • Q1 highlighted the introduction of Derick Elliott and commercial process work; Q2 positioned leadership as an execution accelerator, with Trigg saying Derek Elliott “has marked our next phase of commercial evolution,” alongside the formalized clinical excellence/customer success approach.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management reiterated capital equipment variability and seasonality as ongoing factors. Trigg (CEO Trigg) said “the natural variability of capital sales has made our performance less predictable,” and Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) pointed to Q3 “seasonality.”

  • Confidentiality limits disclosure on the largest announced agreement. Trigg (CEO Trigg) said Outset does “not intend to disclose HCA-specific information today or going forward,” and Gaeta (CFO Gaeta) would not discuss 2027/2028 phasing.

  • Consumables volatility was framed as comp and ordering-timing risk rather than utilization deterioration, with management emphasizing stable utilization visibility and expectations that consumables growth will align with total revenue expectations over the year.

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q2 as a quarter of steadier execution and improving visibility, anchored by reiterated $125M-$130M full-year 2026 revenue guidance, expanding non-GAAP gross margin, and a newly signed $40M HCA refresh agreement extending through 2028. In Q&A, investors’ key debates centered on how sustainable the Q2 console strength is, whether consumables are signaling demand softness, and how much of the HCA agreement will translate into 2027/2028 revenue—questions management addressed with utilization data confidence, seasonality expectations, and confidentiality-driven limits on phasing details.

data.title: INmune Bio targets Ebstrocel U.K. MAA by end of Q3 or early Q4 2026 while outlining $1M-$1.5M monthly burn
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: INmune Bio (INMB) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "For Ebstrocel, we secured formal MHRA alignment, received approval of the pediatric investigation plan, completed a commercial manufacturing milestone, and strengthened our long-term supply chain." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director David Moss) "We now expect to submit Ebstrocel MAA to the MHRA by the end of Q3 or early Q4 '26." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • "The FDA granted Fast Track designation for early Alzheimer's disease, and the Phase 2 MINDFuL study showed a statistically significant treatment effect on white matter myelin MRI biomarkers in the full modified intent-to-treat population." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "The treatment difference was p=0.0028 with a Cohen's effect size of 0.46." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • "The MHRA's official minutes from our May 12th pre-MAA scientific advice meeting confirmed their alignment across every question that we submitted, covering CMC, non-clinical and clinical matters." (Co-Founder, Chair of Scientific Advisory Board, CSO & Chief Manufacturing Officer Mark Lowdell) "The MHRA approved the Ebstrocel pediatric investigation plan in less than 3 months." (Co-Founder, Chair of Scientific Advisory Board, CSO & Chief Manufacturing Officer Lowdell)
  • "Net loss attributable to common stockholders for the quarter ended June 30th, 2026 was approximately $1.3 million." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Cory Ellspermann) "As of June 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $18.4 million." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann) "Based on our current operating plan, we believe our existing cash resources are sufficient to fund operations into the second quarter of 2027." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann)

Outlook

  • "We now expect to submit Ebstrocel MAA to the MHRA by the end of Q3 or early Q4 '26." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "After submitting the MAA in the U.K., we plan to submit the MAA to the EMA in early '27 along with a BLA in the U.S. seeking conditional approval." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • "We plan to submit Ebstrocel Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the first quarter of '27." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "We continue advancing the XPro registrational strategy and evaluating strategic partnerships." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s prepared remarks that said the company "expect[ed] to file for approval beginning in the near term," (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss, Q1) management in Q2 tied the filing to "written MHRA alignment" and specified the MHRA submission window as "end of Q3 or early Q4 '26." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)

Financial Results

  • "Net loss attributable to common stockholders for the quarter ended June 30th, 2026 was approximately $1.3 million compared to approximately $24.5 million" in the year-ago quarter, and management said "[t]he prior period included a $16.5 million impairment charge." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann)
  • "Research and development expenses totaled a benefit of approximately $0.8 million" and management attributed it to "the recognition of additional Australian research and development rebate." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann) "Subsequent to June 30, 2026, we received approximately $4.2 million in Australian research and development tax rebate." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann)
  • "As of June 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $18.4 million" and "as of August 6, 2026, the company had approximately 27.8 million shares of common stock outstanding." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann)

Q&A

  • James Molloy, Alliance Global Partners: On whether the open-label Phase 3 U.S. trial is the previously discussed 12-month safety study; President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss: "Because we are submitting Ebstrocel for conditional approval, we have a follow-on trial that'll be running during the approval process... It's the same one we spoke about earlier." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "No. It's one trial. And it's safety and confirmation trial." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • James Molloy, Alliance Global Partners: On biggest hurdles for U.K./EU filings; President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss: "We're moving forward with itch pain as a primary endpoint." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "we also did in the EBDASI score... pick up the wound scores later in the trial, around the 6-month mark." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • James Molloy, Alliance Global Partners: On confirmatory trial design and timing; President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss: "we expect it to be somewhere around 40 to 45 patients." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "It'll run a total of 18 months" and "we'll have the data right around the middle of '28." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Daniel Carlson (Head of Investor Relations): On focus, pricing, reimbursement; President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss: "the company's focus for the foreseeable future is on the CORDStrom program" (question), and management said, "We expect it's somewhere around GBP 400,000 to GBP 500,000 per year per child." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss) "We will start our pricing negotiations right after we file the MAA." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Daniel Carlson (Head of Investor Relations): On burn and capital strategy; Interim CFO Ellspermann: "our burn rate is maybe $1 million to $1.5 million per month" and noted rebates were "a little bit unusual." (Interim Chief Financial Officer Ellspermann) President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss: "we've got the ATM available" and described funding needs as "little bit here, little bit there." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical and detail-oriented, pressing on trial design and regulatory hurdles (for example, "Is that this or is the 12-month safety trial also going to be running in addition to this?") (James Molloy, Alliance Global Partners)
  • Management tone was positive and execution-focused in prepared remarks ("these achievements materially reduced regulatory and operational risk") and confident in Q&A ("The U.K. is very straightforward, very clear."), with capital-discipline messaging recurring ("We're highly sensitive to dilution"). (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Versus the previous quarter, management’s public tone was more expansive and promotional around timelines, pricing, and capital strategy, while the prior call ended with "we'll not be taking questions." (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss, Q1)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The current call added new, specific regulatory and commercialization markers for Ebstrocel ("submit Ebstrocel MAA... by the end of Q3 or early Q4 '26" and "submit... BLA... in the first quarter of '27"), whereas the prior call emphasized being "approaching a key milestone" without Q&A. (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Q2 elevated XPro’s regulatory positioning with "Fast Track designation" and cited quantitative imaging outcomes ("p=0.0028"; effect sizes "0.46" and "0.59"), while Q1 highlighted ongoing analyses and partner exploration without these metrics. (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Financial runway language moved from "sufficient to fund our operations through Q1 of 2027" (Q1) to "into the second quarter of 2027" (Q2), alongside added discussion of rebates and monthly burn-rate. (Interim Chief Financial Officer Cory Ellspermann)

Risks and Concerns

  • Regulatory and execution timing remained central, with management framing progress as risk reduction: "these achievements materially reduced regulatory and operational risk" ahead of submissions. (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)
  • Manufacturing and supply consistency was positioned as a key platform risk being addressed: "donor variability and manufacturing inconsistency" were cited as persistent MSC challenges, with mitigation via "proprietary donor screening, pooling, and expansion processes" and long-term tissue access. (Co-Founder, Chair of Scientific Advisory Board, CSO & Chief Manufacturing Officer Lowdell)
  • Capital needs and dilution sensitivity were explicitly discussed as a constraint: "we're highly sensitive to dilution" and the company expects to fund with "very small" raises and an "ATM" if needed. (President, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary & Director Moss)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q2 as a quarter of de-risking and timeline specificity for Ebstrocel, citing MHRA alignment, pediatric plan approval, and commercial-ready manufacturing progress, and set expectations for a U.K. MAA submission by end of Q3 or early Q4 2026 followed by EMA and U.S. filings in 2027. On XPro, management highlighted Fast Track status and statistically significant imaging results from MINDFuL, while reiterating partnership evaluation. In Q&A, management detailed a single open-label Phase 3 confirmatory safety trial of about 40 to 45 patients with data expected around mid-2028, discussed U.K. pricing expectations of GBP 400,000 to GBP 500,000 per child per year, and emphasized capital discipline with a stated burn rate of $1 million to $1.5 million per month and an operating runway into Q2 2027.

data.title: NerdWallet expects Q3 revenue of $244M-$260M while scaling IRR-based marketing investment
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: NerdWallet (NRDS) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "We reported revenue of $197 million for the second quarter, up 6% year-over-year" and "Non-GAAP operating income, or NGOI, of $12 million was above the midpoint of our guidance range" (Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Tim Chen).
  • "We're in the middle of an AI transition that is changing how people get their answers to their money questions" and "We're investing in building owned audiences by vertically integrating in some areas and by improving how we register and re-engage with users" (CEO Chen).
  • "The success we are seeing in vertical integration plays across our brokering and advisory business lines is giving us conviction to start investing incremental marketing dollars based on internal rate of return, or IRR, targets rather than solely on in-quarter profitability" and "For the full year 2026, we expect to grow this incremental investment fivefold versus 2025" (CEO Chen).
  • "Consumer revenue was $175 million, up 8% year-over-year" while "SMB revenue was $22 million, down 11% year-over-year" (Chief Financial Officer Jun Lee).
  • "Our trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow grew 100% year-over-year to $141 million, a new record" and "During the quarter, we repurchased $23 million of Class A common stock" (CFO Lee).

Outlook

  • "We expect to deliver third quarter revenue in the range of $244 million to $260 million" and "we expect non-GAAP operating income in the range of $29 million to $37 million" (CFO Lee).
  • "Our Q3 guidance reflects typical seasonality in our business, as well as expected tailwinds from regulatory changes in student loans and the impact of our College Finance acquisition in February" and "we expect our annual profitability to be more concentrated in the third quarter this year than in prior years" (CFO Lee).
  • "For the full year, we're narrowing our NGOI expectation to a range of $90 million to $105 million, maintaining the midpoint of our previous guidance" and "This guidance includes a $15 million to $20 million NGOI impact from customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year" (CFO Lee).
  • Analysts’ estimates were provided, but the JSON fiscal quarter format was not consistent with the required Q1-Q4 validation rules, so no estimates comparison is included.

Financial results

  • "Total revenue in Q2 was $197 million, up 6% year-over-year" and "Consumer revenue was $175 million, up 8% year-over-year" (CFO Lee).
  • "This was partially offset by a decline in consumer credit cards, primarily due to continued organic search headwinds" and "Our largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized, but not yet returned to the level seen earlier in the year" (CFO Lee).
  • "Q2 GAAP operating income was $7 million, and NGOI was $12 million at a 6% margin" and "Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $23 million" (CFO Lee).
  • "As of June 30, we had $62 million of cash and cash equivalents" and "we had $67 million remaining under our share repurchase authorization" (CFO Lee).

Q&A

  • Ralph Schackart, William Blair: asked why NerdWallet is increasing investment "fivefold" with "longer payback duration" and requested payback color; Chief Financial Officer Lee responded, "we're beginning to see cohorts of our consumers with high retention and recurring revenue" and described "an LTV to CAC optimization over a longer period of time while using IRR and payback period as guardrails" (CFO Lee).
  • Ralph Schackart, William Blair: asked about "LLM traffic" and "SEO headwinds"; Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Chen answered, "The traffic is converting well" and "It continues to be a pretty small part of our business today, but it's definitely an area of investment and growth for us" (CEO Chen).
  • Michael Infante, Morgan Stanley: asked about distribution value in an AI future and CAC implications; CEO Chen said, "brand and reach are just an incredible asset" and "Brands with higher trust are going to have advantages" as NerdWallet "banking on" vertical integration (CEO Chen).
  • Michael Infante, Morgan Stanley: asked about SMB being "down 11%" and recovery versus prioritizing consumer vertical integration; CEO Chen said SMB has "2 distinct parts," noting "where we're really seeing headwinds year-over-year is on the non-loans part of the business, and loans is growing year-over-year" and added "we're investing in both" channels/CRM and brokering efficiency (CEO Chen).

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, concentrating on durability of returns and search/AI disruption, including questions on "longer payback duration," "SEO headwinds," and the "path to recovery" in SMB (William Blair; Morgan Stanley).
  • Management tone was slightly positive and investment-focused, emphasizing confidence and positioning, including "we are confident" (Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Tim Chen) and describing IRR discipline as "a capital allocation question" with "a very high bar" (Chief Financial Officer Lee).
  • Versus last quarter’s emphasis on uncertainty from insurance partner monetization, this call’s prepared remarks leaned more toward scaling an IRR-based playbook, while Q&A continued to probe AI/search dynamics.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance frame shifted from Q1’s "we expect to deliver second quarter revenue in the range of $186 million to $202 million" (CFO Lee, prior call) to Q2’s "third quarter revenue in the range of $244 million to $260 million" and "non-GAAP operating income in the range of $29 million to $37 million" (CFO Lee, current call).
  • Investment language evolved from Q1’s "we've decided to be more aggressive in placing our long-term bets" (CEO Chen, prior call) to Q2’s "conviction to start investing incremental marketing dollars based on" IRR and an expectation to grow that incremental investment "fivefold versus 2025" (CEO Chen, current call).
  • Auto insurance commentary moved from Q1’s warning that monetization from "one of our large partners started running below our expectations" (CEO Chen, prior call) to Q2’s update that the "largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized, but not yet returned" (CFO Lee, current call).

Risks and concerns

  • "Organic search headwinds" remained a stated pressure point, affecting "consumer credit cards" and SMB products (Chief Financial Officer Jun Lee).
  • Concentration and volatility in auto insurance persisted, with management noting stabilization but not recovery in its largest carrier relationship and highlighting a mitigation approach: "scaling with other leading auto insurance carriers and expanding our in-house insurance agency" (CFO Lee).
  • The company acknowledged longer paybacks tied to the new investment approach, stating guidance includes an NGOI impact from "customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year" (CFO Lee).

Final takeaway

Management emphasized that Q2 results and updated guidance support a shift toward scaling owned-audience strategies and vertical integration through IRR-based marketing investments, while continuing to navigate organic search headwinds and a not-yet-recovered large auto insurance carrier relationship; leadership framed the AI-driven distribution transition as central to its strategy, pointing to strong cash generation and ongoing share repurchases as it funds longer-payback customer acquisition spend.

data.title: Consensus Cloud reaffirms 2026 revenue of $350M-$364M while outlining Healthcare Strategy group and doc.health tuck-in
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Consensus Cloud Solutions (CCSI) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "We had excellent financial results in Q2, continuing our acceleration of total revenue growth with meaningful contributions from each channel of revenue." (CEO & Director R. Turicchi)
  • "We exceeded our revenue objective with corporate revenue posting a 9.3% growth over Q2 2025 ahead of our forecast." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "Free cash flow was $25.5 million in the quarter" and "we were able to repurchase approximately $9.6 million of our stock during the quarter or approximately 300,000 shares." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "The first is the formation of our new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group headed by Steve Tolle and the second is the tuck-in acquisition of doc.health." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "We will continue to hire into this business unit and its related areas over the balance of the year and into 2027 as we look for meaningful contributions from this group to our non-fax revenue in 2028 and beyond." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "The corporate channel achieved a major milestone, crossing the $60 million mark for the very first time to deliver a record $60.5 million in total revenue for the quarter." (Chief Revenue Officer & Executive VP of Operations Johnny Hecker)
  • "Our NRR continued its upward climb this quarter by more than 1%, reaching 103.1%, up from 102% in Q1." (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "Consolidated revenue of $91.4 million represents an increase of $3.6 million or 4.1% over Q2 2025" and "adjusted EPS of $1.49". (Chief Financial Officer Adam Varon)

Outlook

  • No usable analysts-estimates comparison was included because the provided estimates used a nonstandard quarter format that did not match the required Q1-Q4 validation.
  • "We are reaffirming our full year 2026 outlook" of revenue "$350 million to $364 million," adjusted EBITDA "$182 million to $193 million," and adjusted EPS "$5.55 and $5.95." (CFO Varon)
  • "Moving to Q3 2026 guidance. Revenues between $89.2 million and $93.2 million" with adjusted EBITDA "$45 million" to "$48 million" and adjusted EPS "$1.34 to $1.44." (CFO Varon)
  • "Albeit immaterial, we have incorporated our recent doc.health acquisition into our full year guidance" with impact of "revenues approximately $1 million; EBITDA, negative $0.6 million; EPS, negative $0.02." (CFO Varon)
  • "Based on our first half 2026 performance, Q3 2026 guidance range and acquisition impact, we expect full year revenues to be between the midpoint and high end of the range." (CFO Varon)

Financial Results

  • "Consolidated revenue growing 4.1% year-over-year to $91.4 million." (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $48.3 million" and "a solid 52.9% EBITDA margin". (CFO Varon)
  • "Free cash flow of $25.5 million" and "We ended Q2 2026 with approximately $99 million in cash". (CFO Varon)
  • "Our Board of Directors has authorized an amendment in our equity repurchase plan to approve an increase in the total authorization to $200 million" and "leaving approximately $118 million available". (CFO Varon)
  • "Our Q2 2026 total debt balance stands at approximately $558 million" and "Our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio for Q2 2026 was 2.45x". (CFO Varon)

Q&A

  • Jenny Shen, BTIG, LLC, Research Division: asked whether hospital spending and vendor scrutiny were changing conversations and why full-year guidance was reaffirmed; CRO Hecker said "hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" and "we're emphasizing ROI," while CEO Turicchi said "it is not our practice" to raise annual ranges after quarterly beats and added the company expects to be "between the midpoint and the high end" on revenue and "outperform the midpoint somewhat" on EBITDA and EPS without changing the range. (CRO Hecker; CEO Turicchi)
  • Isaac Sellhausen, Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Research Division: asked for more VA ECFax rollout detail and broader public-sector adoption; CRO Hecker said VA sites are "not a number that we publicly announce or publish" and estimated rollout is "somewhere between 65%, 75%, maybe 80%" while noting "active conversations" with contractors, and said other agencies are progressing but "the government still operates at the pace that it does." (CRO Hecker)
  • Isaac Sellhausen, Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Research Division: asked about hiring and EBITDA margin cadence; CEO Turicchi said headcount is "about 550 employees versus sub-520 when we entered the year" and flagged "an additional $1.3 million of costs" in Q3 tied primarily to audit timing, while stating hires are "primarily in the go-to-market product health care solutions group" and "they're not G&A." (CEO Turicchi)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly negative analyst tone, centered on hospital demand pressure and the decision not to raise guidance: "Have your conversations with hospitals changed at all?" and "What was your decision to reaffirm the full year guide without raising it?" (Jenny Shen, BTIG, LLC, Research Division)
  • Slightly positive management tone in prepared remarks, emphasizing execution and durability, alongside acknowledging buyer friction in health care: "we are pleased to see continued progress" (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker) and "hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" (CRO Hecker).
  • Versus Q1, management kept a consistent guidance posture; Q2 repeated the same principle with CEO Turicchi saying "it is not our practice" to raise the annual range after quarterly beats, aligning with Q1’s "philosophical principle" approach to guidance. (CEO & Director Turicchi)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Corporate growth accelerated from Q1’s "8.2%" year-over-year corporate revenue growth to Q2’s "9.3%". (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • Product and platform messaging progressed from a Q1 "soft launched" rearchitected eFax platform to Q2 "general availability launch of our new eFax platform," plus a Q3 plan for "enhanced mobile capabilities" and an "optional frictionless migration path". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Strategic scope expanded in Q2 with "the formation of our new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group" and the "tuck-in acquisition of doc.health," while Q1 emphasized the platform as an "AI monetization framework" and hiring catch-up. (CEO & Director Turicchi; CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q1’s guidance philosophy question to Q2 scrutiny on hospital spending, VA rollout, and margin cadence, with management repeatedly pointing to execution pacing and internal cost timing drivers. (CEO & Director Turicchi; CRO Hecker)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" and are "more diligent in their vendor selection" with heightened focus on "EHR integration". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "We fully expect to see volatility in net adds, ARPA and total revenue in the SoHo channel" because management will "not chase low-margin volume". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Margin cadence risk was tied to hiring catch-up and cost timing: "you're starting to see the comp expense ramp" and "the bulk of [audit] fees occur in Q3 and Q4" including "an additional $1.3 million of costs" in Q3. (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • A non-operating GAAP item was flagged as volatile: "we, on a GAAP basis, booked a $5.3 million gain on an investment" and "these kind of investments are inherently risky" with future valuation changes "up or down". (CEO & Director Turicchi)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q2 as another quarter of corporate-led growth and high margins while keeping full-year ranges unchanged, pairing that posture with a stepped-up healthcare workflow strategy via a new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group, the doc.health tuck-in, and continued eFax platform rollout. In Q&A, leadership acknowledged slower hospital decision-making and reiterated a guidance philosophy of maintaining annual ranges while positioning full-year results toward the upper portion of the revenue range and slightly above the midpoint for adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS, alongside ongoing capital returns through an expanded $200 million repurchase authorization and a continued VA-driven public-sector rollout.

data.title: Millrose Properties commits up to $1.25B to support Dream Finders' Beazer acquisition
data.description:
Millrose Properties (MRP), a homesite option platform, committed to provide financing of up to $1.25B for Dream Finders Homes' (DFH) $2.2B acquisition of Beazer Homes USA (BZH), the company said Friday. It's the third time since Millrose's founding that the company is providing land-banking capital to support a homebuilder acquisition.

Under the agreement, Millrose plans to acquire homesites from the combined Dream Finders (DFH) and Beazer (BZH) organization, allowing Dream Finders to pursue its capital-light strategy. Dream Finders will maintain option agreements on homesites acquired from Beazer, paying option fees during the development period and purchasing finished homesites over time.

Both homebuilders are Millrose clients and have worked with the company through multiple market cycles, Millrose said.

"Builders across the sector are increasingly turning to Millrose for capital-efficient ways to fund growth, preserve balance sheet flexibility, and position themselves for the long term," said Millrose CEO and President Darren Richman.

Millrose Properties (MRP) stock rose 0.7% in premarket trading.

In Dream Finders' (DFH) announcement of the Beazer acquisition, the company said it expects to finance the transaction through a combination of existing capital resources and committed financing from Goldman Sachs (GS), Bank of America (BAC), and affiliates of Kennedy Lewis Asset Management. 

"Following transaction close, Dream Finders expects to continue executing its growth plans while maintaining its commitment to a 100% land-light strategy," the company said.

data.title: Vital Farms reaffirms 2026 guidance and targets ~$775M-$800M net revenue with ~30% gross margin exit run rate
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Vital Farms (VITL) Q2 2026

Management view

  • “While 2026 presented supply dynamics we did not fully anticipate entering the year, we executed decisively to address them, and the early results give us confidence our operational calibration plan is taking hold.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Russell Diez-Canseco)

  • “We believe the second quarter was our financial trough.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “Our net sales declined 10.1%, but the revenue decline and margin compression we were reporting this quarter are consistent with what we told you to expect on our first quarter call.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “As a result, we delivered a more than 200 basis point year-over-year gain in retail dollar share of the shell egg category during the second quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Since the last earnings call, our price gaps have come down from an average of approximately $2.51 to branded competitors in the first quarter, to an average of $2.36 in the second.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “In the markets where these gaps narrowed, retail volume responded with improved velocity.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Our farmer contract amendments are now live, and our corporate overhead is structurally lower following difficult but necessary cost realignment actions we took during the quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Net revenue in the second quarter declined 10.1% to $166 million.” (CFO Thilo Wrede)

  • “We ended the quarter with $21.2 million in cash and had drawn $30 million against our previous revolving credit line.” (CFO Wrede) “After quarter end, we put in place a new $125 million term loan and a new $60 million asset-based lending facility, replacing our previous revolving facility.” (CFO Wrede)

Outlook

  • “We are reaffirming our previous guidance, which calls for net revenue of $775 million to $800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0 to $10 million.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “We continue to anticipate exiting the fourth quarter at a gross margin run rate of approximately 30%.” (CFO Wrede) “Q3 should mark a sequential improvement in revenue and adjusted EBITDA as breaker volumes abate.” (CFO Wrede)

  • Compared with last quarter’s updated full-year guidance, management reiterated the same ranges: “net revenue of $775 million to $800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0 million to $10 million.” (CFO Wrede, Q1 2026)

  • The “analystsEstimates” tag was not used because it did not provide a valid fiscal-quarter format consistent with the required Q1–Q4 convention.

Financial results

  • “Gross profit was $10.9 million, or 6.6% of net revenue.” (CFO Wrede) “Gross profit includes a $19.5 million impact from excess breaker sales, $0.8 million from the amortization of farmer contract amendments, and $7.8 million in exit costs associated with our butter wind-down.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “SG&A was $40.4 million.” (CFO Wrede) “This includes $3.3 million of restructuring and severance costs, and $3 million in one-time professional services costs related to our feed cost savings program.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $26.6 million.” (CFO Wrede) “The loss for the quarter is a result of the peak intensity supply management costs in Q2, totaling $21.8 million for the quarter.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Full-year supply management costs are now modeled in the mid-$30 million range versus our initial $32 million estimate.” (CFO Wrede) “Importantly, I want to underscore that the contract amendments that are needed for the year are in place.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “At the very beginning of the second quarter, we executed $50 million of share repurchases at an average price of $13.29 per share.” (CFO Wrede) “After the end of the quarter, our board of directors terminated the 2026 stock repurchase plan, consistent with the terms of the new lending facilities.” (CFO Wrede)

Q&A

  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: asked how far the company needs to go on price gaps; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco said, “we are right now is very much on track, we believe, to deliver our full year guidance,” and added, “I don't know that on an overall basis for the entire market, we'll get exactly where we want to be this year.”

  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: asked what’s driving distribution wins; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco emphasized “the core 4 in existing doors” and highlighted a new item: “we launched a new SKU, which is a 24 count at Whole Foods.”

  • Matthew Smith, Stifel: asked about balancing volume growth vs pricing headwind; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco said, “it’s really volume driven from my perspective,” and CFO Wrede pointed to timing, “in fourth quarter, we're dealing with much easier lapping.”

  • Benjamin Mayhew, BMO: asked what the new facilities change; CFO Wrede said the facilities provide flexibility “with $185 million in debt capacity compared to the $60 million that we had before.”

  • Sarang Vora, Telsey: challenged structural margin potential under lower price gaps; CFO Wrede responded, “I don't think we expect anything north of 30,” and said feed savings are intended to “help us pay for the price gap reductions.”

  • Jack Siedow, Needham: asked post-2026 CapEx; CFO Wrede said once through VXR spend, “expect that CapEx spending will fall back down to somewhere of that range,” citing prior “$10 million, $15 million a year.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing, concentrating on price-gap depth, structural margin implications, liquidity, and the credibility of the second-half rebound, including “what gives you confidence that swing is going to work.” (Glenn West, William Blair)

  • Management’s tone in prepared remarks was confident and action-oriented, including “we believe our turnaround plan is working,” and in Q&A remained measured on timing and tradeoffs, including “it reflects the right balance of speed, cost, and seeing a return to positive volume growth.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • Versus last quarter’s more corrective framing—“fall short of our expectations” and “reset of our expectations for 2026” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco, Q1 2026)—this quarter leaned more toward execution evidence and reaffirmation, including “we are reaffirming our full year guidance today.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 emphasized operational proof points—price gap movement to “$2.36,” distribution visibility including “170 to 175 TDPs in the fourth quarter,” and supply actions where “farmer contract amendments are now live.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • Q1 centered on diagnosis and a guidance reset, with management saying “price gaps reached levels that our brand could not sustain,” and cutting full-year guidance to “$775 million to $800 million” net revenue and “$0 to $10 million” adjusted EBITDA. (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco; CFO Wrede)

  • Financing and capital allocation shifted from Q1’s “no debt outstanding” (CFO Wrede, Q1 2026) to Q2’s post-quarter-end borrowing and constraints, including, “our board of directors terminated the 2026 stock repurchase plan.” (CFO Wrede)

Risks and concerns

  • “2026 presented supply dynamics we did not fully anticipate entering the year.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “We may still see some excess breaker sales in the coming quarters, but at a much reduced level than what we experienced in the second quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Shipping and distribution expenses increased to 6.4% of net revenue... reflecting the inclusion of $1.5 million of expenses for shipping excess eggs to breaker plants.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Full-year supply management costs are now modeled in the mid-$30 million range versus our initial $32 million estimate.” (CFO Wrede)

Final takeaway

Management positioned Q2 2026 as the “financial trough,” highlighted narrowing price gaps and expanding distribution as the main drivers for a second-half recovery, and reaffirmed full-year guidance of $775 million to $800 million in net revenue and $0 to $10 million in adjusted EBITDA. The quarter also reflected peak supply-management impacts and a sharp adjusted EBITDA loss, alongside concrete liquidity actions—new debt facilities, a halted repurchase plan, and a controlled CapEx posture—intended to provide runway while supply is rebalanced away from costly breaker volumes.
